definition: Artificial intelligence in customer experience is the use and development of artificial intelligence (AI) to aid and improve customer experience (sometimes abbreviated to CX AI).
details: Chatbots are often seen as the first step in the development of AI within the industry, but more tailored offerings are slowly becoming available. The use of artificial intelligence in the space has since become more diverse than simply chatbots, with AI underpinning entire CX cloud platforms now used at major corporations. Contact center as a service (CCaaS) has become a core solution of the CX (customer experience) industry, with the CCaaS market size expected to reach $17.19 Billion by 2030 in the United States alone.

explainer.lead: Artificial intelligence in customer experience, sometimes called CX AI, uses AI to support and improve how customers are served. Its role has grown from chatbots into tailored offerings and AI-supported cloud platforms used by major corporations.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a shop helper that answers questions on a computer instead of at a counter. At first, that helper might be a chatbot, but it can become part of a bigger set of tools that helps a whole company look after its customers. The main idea is to use AI to make customer experiences better.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer may encounter CX AI as a chatbot, a more tailored offering, or one capability within a CX cloud platform. Contact center as a service (CCaaS) is a core industry setting. A common pitfall is scoping the work as chatbot deployment alone when the intended use is platform-wide customer experience support.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, CX AI denotes the use and development of artificial intelligence to aid and improve customer experience, rather than a specific model or algorithm. Its scope spans chatbots, tailored offerings, AI-underpinned CX cloud platforms, and CCaaS. The term specifies an application area and objective, not a training method or evaluation metric.

explainer.example: A customer asks a company's chatbot, “Where is my order?” and the AI handles the initial response. In a larger deployment, that chatbot can be one part of an AI-supported CX cloud platform rather than the whole customer-experience system.

explainer.intuition: CX AI applies artificial intelligence to customer service and support, with the goal of improving the customer's experience. It can range from a single chatbot to AI supporting an entire customer-experience platform.
howItWorks: Start with a customer-service or support interaction.
Apply AI through a chatbot or a more tailored offering.
Extend AI support across a broader CX cloud platform when needed.
Use CCaaS as a core contact-center solution within the CX industry.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI can support customer experience at platform scale, not merely automate individual chats. CCaaS has become a core CX solution, and its United States market is expected to reach $17.19 billion by 2030.
misconceptions: CX AI means only chatbots; its uses have become more diverse.
Chatbots are the final stage; they are often seen as a first step.
CX AI is one particular algorithm; it is a broad application area.
